<action type="say">
Good—blocking it and ordering a replacement was the critical first step.

Here’s the **order of operations** and language you can use, plus what to do about the rest of your wallet and ID.

---

### 1) Capture details of the suspicious charges

In your app / web:

1. Open the **stolen credit card account → Recent activity / Transactions**.
2. For each charge you don’t recognize, note:
   - **Date & time**
   - **Merchant name**
   - **Amount**
   - **Status** (pending/posted)
3. Take **screenshots** or write them down.

You’ll reference this exactly when you talk to the bank.

---

### 2) Dispute the 3 suspicious transactions

#### Option A – Dispute directly in the app (if available)

On the suspicious charge, see if there’s a link like:

- “**Report a problem**”
- “**Dispute transaction**”
- “Don’t recognize this charge?”

If so, tap it and use language like:

- **Reason/description field:**

  > “My wallet and card were stolen on [date, e.g., July 29, 2026]. I did not authorize this transaction or give my card or number to anyone. Please treat this as fraud and remove the charge.”

Repeat for each unauthorized transaction.

#### Option B – Call/chat with the bank

Call the number on the app (often **Help / Contact us / Call**). When connected, you can say:

> “My credit card was stolen earlier tonight and I’ve already reported it as stolen and had it blocked. I’m now seeing several charges I don’t recognize from this evening that I did not authorize. I need to dispute those as fraudulent.”

Then give specifics:

> “The transactions are:
>  - [Date, time] – [Merchant name] – [$X.XX]
>  - [Date, time] – [Merchant name] – [$X.XX]
>  - [Date, time] – [Merchant name] – [$X.XX]
>
> I did not make these, no one else is authorized on my card, and my physical card and wallet are missing.”

Ask them explicitly:

> “Can you open fraud disputes for each of those, and confirm whether I’ll see provisional credits and when?”

If any are **pending**, ask:

> “For the pending transactions, can you stop them from posting, or will they post and then be reversed through the dispute?”

---

### 3) Lock down everything else from the stolen wallet

Run through this quickly:

1. **Other bank / credit cards in the wallet**
   - For **each** card from any bank:
     - Log into that bank’s app or site.
     - Either:
       - **Lock/freeze** the card immediately, then
       - Use “**Report card lost/stolen**” and request a **replacement**.
   - Do not wait—even if you don’t see bad charges yet.

2. **Debit card(s)**
   - Same process: **lock/freeze**, then **report lost/stolen**.
   - Ask the bank to **monitor or block ATM withdrawals** and issue a new debit card and possibly a new card number.

3. **Driver’s license / state ID**
   - Look up your state DMV’s process for **reporting a lost/stolen license**.
   - File the report and request a **replacement ID**.
   - This doesn’t usually stop them from using your name/address, but it creates a paper trail.

4. **Health insurance card / other ID cards**
   - If a **health insurance card** was in the wallet, call the insurer:
     - Report it lost and ask for a **new member ID** if they recommend it.
   - Same idea for **work ID/access card**—contact your employer to **deactivate** it.

5. **If any passwords/PINs were in the wallet (written down)**
   - Immediately change:
     - **Online banking password**
     - **Primary email password**
     - Any password that might have been written in the wallet.

---

### 4) Identity & credit protection (since your ID was in the wallet)

These steps are more cautious but smart:

1. **Place a fraud alert** on your credit file (free):
   - Contact **one** of the major bureaus (Experian, Equifax, TransUnion); they’ll notify the others.
   - Say:

     > “My wallet, including my ID and credit cards, was stolen. I want to place a fraud alert on my credit file.”

2. **Pull and review your credit reports**:
   - Look for any **new accounts** or **inquiries** you don’t recognize.
   - If you see something off, we can walk through language for disputing that too.

3. **Consider a credit freeze** (optional but stronger):
   - You request a **credit freeze** with each bureau if you want to make it very hard to open new accounts in your name.

---

### 5) Quick script to summarize everything to your bank’s fraud team

If they ask you to explain the situation in one go:

> “My entire wallet was stolen on [date] in [city/area]. I’ve already reported my credit card as stolen and it’s now blocked with a replacement on the way. I’ve just noticed these charges from tonight that I did not make and that no one is authorized to make. I want to dispute each of them as fraud and ensure I’m not held responsible for any unauthorized activity, including anything that might still be pending.”

---

If you tell me:
- The **dates/amounts** of the 3 charges, and
- Whether there were **other cards or your driver’s license** in the wallet,

I can turn this into a super short personalized checklist you can save and just tick through.</action>

2) Quick checklists for the other debit card, other credit card, and license

**A. Debit card (other bank card in the wallet)**

- [ ] Log into that bank’s **app or website**.
- [ ] Go to **Accounts → [Debit/Checking] → Card management / Card controls**.
- [ ] **Lock/freeze** the debit card immediately (if option exists).
- [ ] Use **“Report card lost/stolen”** (or call the bank’s 24/7 number from the app/site).  
  Script:

- [ ] Then use **“Report card lost or stolen”** / “Replace card.”

- [ ] Go to your **state DMV** website (or search: `<Your State> DMV report lost stolen license`).
- [ ] Follow the online process or note if you must **call or visit**.
- [ ] File it as **lost/stolen** and request a **replacement license/ID**.
- [ ] If there’s a field for explanation, you can write:

  > “Entire wallet stolen on [date]; requesting replacement license and noting prior license as lost/stolen.”

- [ ] Keep any **reference/confirmation number**.
- [ ] Consider:
  - [ ] Placing a **fraud alert** with a credit bureau since your ID + cards were stolen.
